one_liner: Senior analyst building budget models, workforce cost estimates and financial-management plans as the federal Judiciary seeks authority to own and manage its own buildings.
fit_summary: Daniel's IEM consulting work for government clients and policy knowledge may touch briefings and stakeholder coordination, but this is a senior (about $169K+) budget and financial-management role. It requires a full year of specialized experience in ALL three areas: organizational change plans with cost/benefit analysis, executive-level analysis, and federal acquisition knowledge. Unless Daniel's IEM duties included federal budgeting, cost estimating or contract work, Daniel likely won't meet the minimum qualifications.
eligibility: Open to the public as well as competitive and excepted federal employees; no status or veterans' preference is needed, but you must be a U.S. citizen for a competitive-status appointment.

You need at least 52 weeks of specialized experience covering ALL listed areas: organizational change plans (workforce analysis, organizational design, change management, risk and cost/benefit analysis), unstructured analysis and briefings for senior executives, and knowledge of federal acquisition (IT, real property and financial management services contracts, contractor staffing).
No degree is required, and no security clearance is required.
You must pass an FBI fingerprint check, a public trust suitability check and E-Verify, complete the OF-306, and serve a trial period as a first-time federal appointee.
Mandatory narrative responses are required; leaving them out costs you full consideration.
strategy: Before applying, write down honestly what you did at IEM. Apply only if you can point to at least 52 weeks covering all three specialized-experience areas; the questionnaire ratings will be checked against your resume.

Frame IEM work by function, not firm. Name any federal clients (for example FEMA or other agencies), contract type, budget or cost-estimating tasks, staffing plans, and briefings delivered to government executives.

Use your two-page USAJOBS resume to give each job dates, hours per week and a brief specialized-experience statement that mirrors the three required areas. Use the posting's exact phrases, such as cost/benefit analysis and gap analysis.
Write the mandatory narratives with STAR examples tied to each required area. Answer the questionnaire only at the level your resume clearly supports.
Submit well before the November 3, 2026 deadline (the posting opens October 20).

If you don't qualify, use this posting to steer toward FEMA, emergency management or legislative/policy analyst roles at GS-9 to GS-12, or Prince William County and Virginia emergency management jobs.
resume_bullets: Developed [cost/benefit or workforce cost estimates] for [federal/state client] [emergency management/recovery program], analyzing [staffing, contract and equipment costs] to support [decision/outcome] ([dates], [hours]/week).
Prepared and delivered [number] written analyses and briefings to [senior executives/agency officials] on [topic], supporting decisions on [organizational structure/resource allocation].
Supported federal contract [requirements development/deliverable management/invoice review] on [contract name/type], coordinating contractor staff and government stakeholders to [result].
interview_questions: Describe how you built a multi-year budget or cost model for an organizational change. What assumptions drove it?
How would you decide which functions should be done by government employees versus contractors?
Tell us about a time you briefed senior executives on a complex, unstructured problem with incomplete data.
Walk us through how you would run a gap analysis of the financial-management workload created by a new real property authority.
watch_outs: The specialized experience requires ALL three areas, including federal acquisition knowledge. Self-rating higher than your resume supports will lower your rating or disqualify you.
The salary level signals a senior, budget-heavy role, and the 'highly desired' list includes 10+ years of federal financial management, which favors experienced federal budget analysts.
The job is in DC and not remote; telework is available, but expect a commute from Manassas.
The posting is open only October 20 to November 3, 2026, a two-week window.
